question: A 37-year-old woman comes to the physician because of oligomenorrhea and intermittent vaginal spotting for 5 months. Menses previously occurred at regular 28-day intervals and lasted for 5 days with normal flow. She has also noted increased hair growth on her chin. She is not sexually active. She takes no medications. Physical examination shows temporal hair recession and nodulocystic acne on her cheeks and forehead. There is coarse hair on the chin and the upper lip. Pelvic examination shows clitoral enlargement and a right adnexal mass. Laboratory studies show increased serum testosterone concentration; serum concentrations of androstenedione and dehydroepiandrosterone are within the reference ranges. Ultrasonography of the pelvis shows a 10-cm right ovarian tumor. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
analysis: The most likely diagnosis in this case is a Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor, also known as an androblastoma. This type of tumor can produce androgens, leading to symptoms such as hirsutism, clitoromegaly, and menstrual irregularities. The presence of clitoral enlargement, elevated serum testosterone levels, and an ovarian mass are all suggestive of a Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor.
